correctness.rationale: The p-semigroup gaps are exactly jp+i with i>=1 and i+j<=p-2, in particular p never divides a gap. In the formal gluing quotient logarithmic differentiation takes multiplication to addition. Units in the smooth-chart ring contribute only nonpositive powers, whereas units in the cusp completed ring contribute only semigroup powers. Thus the gap coefficients descend on arbitrary base rings. In the chart 1+sum c_g T^g the gap-coordinate map is triangular with diagonal -g, giving a section; its image is closed and full-dimensional in the smooth connected (therefore integral) Picard scheme, so the section is an isomorphism. Independently, the chain rule for T'=T/(1+aT^(1-p)) gives (1+aT^(1-p))^(-1) W(T'). The a^m coefficient at exponent g=jp+i is (-1)^m binom(g+mp,m) w_(g+m(p-1)), reduced to binom(i,m) for 0<=m<p. For m=i the input index is p(j+i), and the formal unit factorization gives w_(pt)=w_t^p universally, not just for a perfect coefficient field. The first-order coefficient at i>=2 reaches exactly all higher-row gaps, and i=1 gives each first-row p-th power. These equations kill every higher coefficient as well (either use the displayed binomial expansion or the restricted-exponential coaction). The surviving coordinates are additive, so the group scheme is alpha_p^(p-2), including its full nilpotent structure. The elliptic diagonal quotient has the setup in the cited Picard theorem and the smooth-chart point u=0 is fixed; apply Corollary 5.2. The finite subgroup is already infinitesimal. The case p=3 has one gap and one p-th-power equation. The frozen finite-prime checker was read but not run, and no finite run is needed for the coaction identities.
